strokesGained.note: Tee-to-green SG is per-shot over recorded shots (penalties & un-sensed shots excluded). Buckets are distance-based (offTee = par4/5 tee; long 150+, mid 50-150, inside-50). sg0to100 is the leverage metric (100yd-and-in, no putts). Putting is count-based (3-putts penalized; totalPutts/threePutts authoritative).

reconciliation.note: Score is authoritative. The sensor shot layer is imperfect: it can under-record (un-sensed short shots; penalties carry no position) or over-record (phantom/practice strokes). Treat shot counts as spatial detail, not stroke truth; discount suspectHoles for club/distance stats. Counts here EXCLUDE phantomShots (between-hole transit logged as strokes); those shots stay in `holes[].shots` flagged with phantom=true.

annotations.narrative:
# Overall

## Approach to the round
Felt loose. Hummed Mr. Jones in head to calm nerves and bring me to a Back Nine Mental Space.  Tried to appreciate the walk in between, did not obsess over score.  Only focused on clean backswing and visualizing the ball flight in advance along with throwing the club down the line.  After Analyst, added follow-through to that list as I was pushing right on a few and that helped overall.  Used club data 'actual yardage' from the 'The Turn'. Generally over clubbed as needed but had several shots in the ~160ish range where I have a 7i ~140 and 9W ~180-200 -- used the 6i as well and performed well.  I started lining up on the tee box on the side with my miss so I would angle away from it.  

## Foundations
- Putting was really good -- felt very confident, Number of putts is misleading as I sunk many two putts which would have been three in other rounds from 6-10'. I adopted a slightly more aggressive putt on shorter putts to hit with confidence and if I leave 3' past so be it, at least not short, working really well. Was complimented by both Ed and Steve on putting. 
- Driver - Very good -- Zero penalties due to driver. Only hit dead straight once, but had a predictable fade. I probably need to aim with that more. Often I hit a solid drive but fade would land me in tree cover causing rescue, should have accepted earlier and started aim down left side of fairway.
- Pitching - ok -- good earlier in round, but found a real miss pattern for me which is uphill lie when on the hill going up to green. Consistently hitting way short. Also learned that on dead bermuda, it is hard (like hitting off granite) and the lack of give screwed up several shots -- need to learn a strategy for that.
- Long Clubs - Good -- 9W was a star today , really hitting well. 4 hybrid not bad, no complaints but not the best they have ever been
- Irons - Really interesting today -- so I have calibrated my distance down to use 'The Turn' club data, but must have been hitting very clean as sailed over green several times - four times where I went way past.  Not sure if I am finally getting used to new irons or simply had a very flush day with them.  Only real mishits were on Hole 3.  I found taking the more horizontal swing plane approach really allows clean shots and will work that more into range round -- took the thinking out and was hitting very well (unfortunately paid price with too much distance but not the worst problem to have moving forward I can recalibrate as needed)

## Specific Holes

### H4 - Double (Par 5)
Great drive (first driver of day) - 214, a bit down left side but fine.  Followed with a nice 198y 5W to left of green. Wedged over trap onto fringe, three putted.

### H5 - Double (Par 3)
This one was frustrating as this hole is surrounded by bunkers and always gives me trouble. Even though a par 3 I tried to play smart by hitting around 100 yard Pitch shot leaving me 50y to green. Unfortunately it is downhill and rolled into creek bet when I sent it 108.  This one is ~165y and I don't have a ton of confidence in that shot so thought I was playing smart to avoid bunkers, but stung me this time costing penalty.  Pitched on back side of green with 2 putts to finish (only penalty of day)

### H6 - Double (Par 4)
- Monster drive at 274, and this is where the irons going too long started. Hit great clean 8i up the line expecting 128y but sending over green back side of hill at about 145 -- very tough recovery under trees onto small green.  Sent the punhch a bit too far, 3 putted from 70'

### H8 - Double (Par 4)
- Tee boxes up further this time which was nice, hit a great 9W 192y up the left side of of dogleg to have a good approach. Avoided trees and trouble. Took my 9i out expecting 120ish yard shot -- went 145 with another just solid hit right at the pin but too far over. Had to recover from in woods with a low punch with 2 putts.


### H10 - Bogey (Par 3)
- About 165y -- used my 6i -- ripped it and went over back hill, likely hit cart path - ended up 222y. Under trees wedged up and 2 putts.

### H11 - Double (Par 3)
- Hit 7i 10y further than expected and pulled left, not major trouble. Wedged twice followed by 2 putts.

### H13 - Birdie (Par 5)
- Drive 251y, pretty hard fade behind some trees, but had a decent approach from the right, so took my 6i and had a low shot 132y, left a clean approach with a nice 96y PW. Putted from rough and sunk with one putt.

### H15 - Double (Par 4)
- Nice Drive 217y in fairway. Hit nice 5W 182y to left of green near sandtrap.  Think heat and fatigue hitting. On the Uphill lie wedge duffed very short, hit again, but was thin and shot across green, 2 putt.

### H16 - Triple (Par 4)
Felt like a blowup.
- Hit a nice driver 237y, followed by a nice 9W 161y to the right of green.  Wedges sucked here. Hit too far 48y over green, Used putter from here even well off green as I had lost confidence in wedges with 2 real putts but one putt from rough.
